plain_english: Now the ninth chapter. The blessed Lord said: I will declare to the non-envious this most secret knowledge together with realized knowledge; knowing it, you will be freed from the inauspicious. Non-enviousness is the chief cause in the transmission of knowledge, as before in knowledge and realization.
sanskrit_cite: atha navamo'dhyāyaḥ   śrībhagavānuvāca   idaṃ tu te guhyatamaṃ pravakṣyāmyanasūyave | jñānaṃ  vijñānasahitaṃ yajjñātvā mokṣyase'śubhāt | anasūyatvaṃ jñānasaṃkrāntau kāraṇaṃ mukhyam | jñānavijñāne-prāgvat

plain_english: This royal, secret, pure, supreme knowledge is directly perceived, righteous, easy to do, and imperishable; it shines among all knowledges and is called self-knowledge. Kings such as Janaka have authority in it; because it is greatly hidden it is secret, and because of heroic kshatriya steadiness it is very easy to do and perform; and its brahma-worship action entails no expenditure like other actions through enjoyment.
sanskrit_cite: rājavidyā rājaguhyaṃ pavitramidamuttamam | pratyakṣāvagamaṃ  dharmyaṃ susukhaṃ kartumavyayam | rājate-sarvavidyāmadhye dīpyate yā | ihaiva hyucyate-adhyātmavidyā  vidyānām iti | rājñām-janakādīnāmatrādhikārasteṣāṃ  rahasyam-atiguptatvāt kṣatriyasulabhena vīrabhāvenāvikampatvāt | kartum-anuṣṭhātuṃ susukham | na cāsya brahmopāsanātmanaḥ  karmaṇo'nyakarmavadupabhogādinā vyayo'sti

plain_english: Men without faith in this dharma, O scorcher of foes, do not attain me; they turn back on the path of death and saṃsāra, being born again and again and dying.
sanskrit_cite: aśraddadhānāḥ puruṣā dharmasyāsya parantapa | aprāpya māṃ  nivartante mṛtyusaṃsāravartmani | nivartante-punaḥpunarjāyante mriyante ca

plain_english: I pervade this whole world in unmanifest form; all beings stand in me, yet I am not situated in them. Even considering for long that all beings stand in me, there is no other support-abode; in their appearance, the opposite knowledge-nature is concealed by making inert form preceded by the known self-nature. Thus it is said: I am not situated in them.
sanskrit_cite: mayā tatamidaṃ kṛtsnaṃ jagadavyaktamūrtinā | matsthāni  sarvabhūtāni na cā'haṃ teṣvavasthitaḥ | matsthāni sarvabhūtānīti-suciramapi gatvā anyasya  pratiṣṭhādhāmno'vidyamānatvāt | bhūtarūpabodhyātmakaprasiddhatadīyajaḍarūpapuraḥsarīkāreṇa  tadavabhāse tadviparītabodhasvabhāvatirodhānam | ityetadāha-na  cāhaṃ teṣvavasthitaḥ-iti

plain_english: Beings do not dwell in me; see my divine yoga. I bear beings, yet my self, though sustaining beings, does not dwell in them. The ignorant, blind to truth, think the supreme Lord is limited, seeing only a finite self on earth; but the Lord's yoga is unsurpassed sovereign freedom.
sanskrit_cite: na ca matsthāni bhūtāni paśya me yogamaiśvaram | bhūtabhṛnna ca  bhūtastho mamātmā bhūtabhāvanaḥ | na ca matsthāni-avidyāndhānāṃ tattvādṛṣṭeḥ | nahi mūḍhā  avicchinnasaṃvitsvabhāvaṃ parameśvaraṃ  samastavastuparicchedapratiṣṭhāsthānaṃ manyante | apitu kṛśo  devadatto'ham idaṃ vedmi bhūtale idaṃ sthitam-iti mitameva  svabhāvaṃ pratiṣṭhā-sthānatayā paśyanti | nanu  kathametadviruddham ? ityāha- paśya me yogamaiśvaram-iti | yogaḥ-śaktiḥ-yujyamānatvāt | etadeva mamaiśvaryaṃ-yadevaṃ  niratiśayādbhutavṛttisvātantryamityarthaḥ

plain_english: Just as the great, all-pervading wind ever abides in space, so know that all beings abide in me.
sanskrit_cite: yathākāśasthito nityaṃ vāyuḥ sarvatrago mahān | tathā sarvāṇi  bhūtāni matsthānītyupadhāraya

plain_english: Thus indeed I move unseen in all beings, resting on being-nature, together and without; as space and wind remain inseparable yet sky is never touched, so the Lord's principle, though spread through all world, is not an object for everyone.
sanskrit_cite: evaṃ hi sarvabhāveṣu carāmyanabhilakṣitaḥ | bhūtaprakṛtimāsthāya sahaiva ca vinaiva ca | yadvadākāśavāyvoravinābhāvinyapi saṃbandhe na jātucinnabhaḥ  spṛśyatā śrūyate evaṃ sakalasaṃsāravisāryapi bhagavattattvaṃ  na sarvajanaviṣayam

plain_english: All beings, son of Kunti, go to my nature at world-dissolution; again at world-beginning I emit those beings into unmanifest nature.
sanskrit_cite: sarvabhūtāni kaunteya prakṛtiṃ yānti māmikām | kalpakṣaye  punastāni kalpādau visṛjāmyaham | prakṛtim-avyaktarūpām

plain_english: Taking hold of my own nature, I emit again and again this entire helpless group of beings by nature's control; by this much, even this inert group of beings has obtained manifestness through connection with the higher nature.
sanskrit_cite: prakṛtiṃ svāmavaṣṭabhya visṛjāmi punaḥ punaḥ | bhūtagrāmamimaṃ kṛtsnamavaśaṃ prakṛtervaśāt | svāṃ prakṛtimavaṣṭabhya-ityetāvatā jaḍo'pi svato'yaṃ  bhāvagrāmaḥ paraprakṛtyanvayātprakāśatāṃ prāptaḥ

plain_english: Those actions do not bind me, wealth-winner, seated like an indifferent one, unattached in those actions.
sanskrit_cite: na ca māṃ tāni karmāṇi nibadhnanti dhanañjaya | udāsīnavadāsīnamasaktaṃ teṣu karmasu

plain_english: With me as overseer, nature produces moving and still things; by this cause, son of Kunti, the world revolves. There is no action-bondage for me by indifference, because I exist; therefore I am cause in world-creation without relying on activity.
sanskrit_cite: mayādhyakṣeṇa prakṛtiḥ sūyate sacarācaram | hetunānena kaunteya  jagad viparivartate | na ca me'sti karmabandhaḥ-audāsītyena vartamāno'haṃ yataḥ | ata  evāhaṃ jagannirmāṇe'nāśritavyāpāratvāddhetuḥ

plain_english: Fools despise me dwelling in human body, not knowing the supreme imperishable being; I lie within all people, yet the Lord beyond the fourteen kinds, including human, is not found, so how does he exist?
sanskrit_cite: avajānanti māṃ mūḍhā mānuṣīṃ tanumāsthitam | paraṃ  bhāvamajānanto mamāvyayamanuttamam | so'haṃ sarvajanāntaḥśāyī  sarvasyātmapararūpatayāvajñāspadam-yanmānuṣādi-caturdaśavidhasa  rgavyatirikta īśvaro nopalabhyate sa kathamastīti

plain_english: Those of demonic and rakshasic nature have vain hopes, actions, and knowledge; their karma, knowledge, and desire are fruitless because directed to non-reality.
sanskrit_cite: moghāśā moghakarmāṇo moghajñānā vicetasaḥ | āsurīṃ  rākṣasīṃ caiva prakṛtiṃ mohinīṃ śritāḥ | teṣāṃ ca karma jñānamākāṅkṣāśca sarvaṃ  niṣphalam-avastuviṣayatvāt | āsurīṃ rākṣasīṃ  ceti-udriktarajastamodharmāṇa iti

plain_english: Great souls, resorting to divine nature, worship with unwavering mind, knowing the imperishable origin of beings.
sanskrit_cite: mahātmānastu māṃ pārtha daivīṃ prakṛtimāśritāḥ | bhajantyananyamanaso jñātvā bhūtādimavyayam

plain_english: Always glorifying, striving, vowed, bowing, and ever united, they worship with devotion.
sanskrit_cite: satataṃ kīrtayantaśca yatantaśca yatavratāḥ | namasyantaśca māṃ  bhaktyā nityayuktā upāsate

plain_english: Some worship by knowledge-sacrifice as one, others by external offerings in many ways; all are devoted to the Lord.
sanskrit_cite: jñānayajñena cā'pyanye yajanto māmupāsate | ekatvena pṛthaktvena  bahudhā viśvatomukham | daivīṃ-sāttvikīm | yajanto-bāhyadravyādiyāgaiḥ | anye tu māṃ  jñānayajñenaivopāsate | ataḥ kecit ekatayā-jñānataḥ | kecid  bahudhā-karmayogāt | matparā eva sarve | nanu karma tāvatkārakakalāpavyāptabhedodreki kathamabhinnaṃ  bhagavatpadaṃ prāpayatīti ? ucyate-

plain_english: I am sacrifice, svadha, medicine, mantra, ghee, fire, and offering.
sanskrit_cite: ahaṃ kraturahaṃ yajñaḥ svadhāhamahamauṣadham | mantro'hamahamevājyamahamagnirahaṃ hutam

plain_english: I am father, mother, supporter, and grandfather of this world; I am the knowable, purifier, om, rig, sama, and yajur.
sanskrit_cite: pitāhamasya jagato mātā dhātā pitāmahaḥ | vedyaṃ  pavitramoṅkāra ṛksāma yajureva ca

plain_english: The Lord is the goal, supporter, witness, dwelling, refuge, friend, origin, dissolution, abode, treasure, and imperishable seed.
sanskrit_cite: gatirbhartā prabhuḥ sākṣī nivāsaḥ śaraṇaṃ suhṛt | prabhavaḥ  pralayaḥ sthānaṃ nidhānaṃ bījamavyayam

plain_english: The Lord heats, withholds, and releases; is nectar and death, being and nonbeing; one partless principle supports all action.
sanskrit_cite: tapāmyahamahaṃ varṣaṃ nigṛhṇāmyutsṛjāmi ca | amṛtaṃ caiva  mṛtyuśca sadasaccāhamarjuna | ekasyaiva nirbhāgasya brahmatattvasya parikalpitasādhanādhīnaṃ  karmapunarekatvaṃ nirvartayati-kriyāyāḥ  sarvakārakātmasākṣātkāreṇāvasthāne bhagavatpadaprāptiṃ  pratyavidūratvāt | uktaṃ ca-   seyaṃ kriyātmikā śaktiḥ śivasya paśuvartinī | bandhayitrī  svamārgasthā jñātā siddhyupapādikā | (spa0, 3 ni0, 16 ślo0)   iti | mayāpyuktaṃ-   upakrame yaiva buddhirbhāvābhāvānuyāyinī | upasaṃhṛtikāle sā  bhāvābhāvānuyāyinī | iti tatra tatra vitatya vicāritacarametat itīhoparamyate | taṣāmyahamityādi-advaitakathāprasaṅgenoktam | nanvevaṃ yadi bāhyayāgādināpi brahmāptiḥ  tarhyagniṣṭomādiṣvapi kimanyo yājyaḥ ? abhyupagame bhedavādaḥ  vāsudeva eveti cet kathaṃ nāpavargastaiḥ ? tadarthamucyate-

plain_english: Knowers of the three Vedas, purified of sin, sacrifice and seek heaven; gaining merit, they enjoy divine pleasures in Indra's world.
sanskrit_cite: traividyā māṃ somapāḥ pūtapāpā yajñairiṣṭvā svargatiṃ  prārthayante | te puṇyamāsādya surendraloka- maśnanti divyāndivi  devabhogān

plain_english: They enjoy vast heaven, then return to the mortal world when merit is exhausted; desire limits the fruit, so they come and go.
sanskrit_cite: te taṃ bhuktvā svargalokaṃ viśālaṃ kṣīṇe puṇye martyalokaṃ  viśanti | evaṃ trayīdharmamanuprapannā gatāgataṃ kāmakāmā  labhanta | yadyapi te māmeva yajante tathāpi svargamātraprārthanayā  mitakarmanijasattvadurbalatayā svargādimātreṇaiva  phalenāvacchindanti | ata evaiṣāṃ punarāvartako dharmaḥ | evaṃ te  gatāgataṃ labhante natu yāgasya punarāvṛttiprasavadharmā  svabhāvaḥ | tathāhi

plain_english: For those who worship without other thought, the Lord carries yoga and security; yoga is gaining one's own form, security is protecting gained divine form.
sanskrit_cite: ananyāścintayanto māṃ ye janāḥ paryupāsate | teṣāṃ  nityābhiyuktānāṃ yogakṣemaṃ vahāmyaham | tebhyo'nye māṃ cintayantaḥ katham? ananyā-avidyamānam  anyat-madvyatiriktaṃ kāmanīyaṃ phalaṃ yeṣāmiti | yogaḥ-apratilabdhamatsvarūpalābhaḥ | kṣemaṃ-prāptabhagavatsvarūpapratiṣṭhālābhaparirakṣaṇam | yena  yogabhraṣṭatvaśaṅkāpi na bhavedityarthaḥ

plain_english: Even devotees of other gods, endowed with faith, sacrifice; they too worship me, Kaunteya, though without proper rule.
sanskrit_cite: ye'pyanyadevatābhaktā yajante śraddhayānvitāḥ | te'pi māmeva  kaunteya yajantyavidhipūrvakam

plain_english: I am the enjoyer and lord of all sacrifices, yet they do not know me truly and therefore deviate.
sanskrit_cite: ahaṃ hi sarvayajñānāṃ bhoktā ca prabhureva ca | natu  māmabhijānanti tattvenātaścalanti te

plain_english: God-vowed go to gods, ancestor-vowed to ancestors, being-worshippers to beings, and my worshippers to me.
sanskrit_cite: yānti devavratā devānpitṛnyānti pitṛvratāḥ | bhūtāni yānti  bhūtejyā yānti madyājino'pi mām

plain_english: Offerings made with devotion are accepted, and even worship under other names reaches me, since nothing worshippable exists apart from brahman; the difference lies in proper or improper rite.
sanskrit_cite: patraṃ puṣpaṃ phalaṃ toyaṃ yo me bhaktyā prayacchati | tadahaṃ  bhaktyupahṛtamaśnāmi prayatātmanaḥ | ye'pi ca nāmadheyāntarairupāsate te'pi māmevopāsate | nahi  brahmavyatireki kiṃcidupāsyamasti | kintu-avidhineti viśeṣaḥ | avidhiḥ-anyo vidhiḥ nānāprakārairvidhibhirahameva  paraṃbrahmasattāsvabhāvo yājya iti | natu  yathānyairdarśanāntaradūṣaṇasamupārjitamahāpātakamalīmasairvya  akha-khatam-avidhinā-duṣṭavidhineti | evaṃ hi sati māmeva yajante  sarvayajñānāṃ cāhameva bhoktā-iti  dṛśyamānametadasamañjasībhavet | ityalaṃ kalmaṣakalilaiḥ sākaṃ  saṃlāpena | asmadguravastu nirūpayanti-anyā-svātmavyatiriktā  bhedavādanayena brahmasvabhāvahīnaiva kāciddevatā-iti gṛhītvā  tāmeva yajante | te'pi vastuto māmeva-svātmarūpaṃ yajante kintu  avidhinā-duṣṭena vidhinā bhedagrahaṇarūpeṇeti | ata evāha-natu  māṃ-svātmānaṃ tattvena-devatārūpatayā bhoktṛtvena jānanti  ataḥ calante-madrūpāt | kiṃ devavratatvena devānyānti-ityādi  etadeva calanamiti yāvat | ye tu matsvarūpamabhedena viduste  devabhūtapitṛyāgādināpi māmeva yajante | te ca madyājino māmeva  gacchantītyupasaṃhariṣyati | nanu dravyatyāgārthamuddiṣṭā  devatetyucyate tatkathamanuddiśya svātmatattvasya yājyatvam ādityaḥ  prāpaṇīyaḥ caruḥ-iti  vidhiśeṣabhūtadevatoddeśātmakavidhyantarabhāvito hyasāvuddeśaḥ | na ca svātmaviṣayo vidhirasti-ityabhiprāyeṇāha avidhipūrvakaṃ  māmiti | svātmavyatiriktāyāṃ devatāyāmasti apekṣyo  vidhiḥ-aprāptaprāpaṇarūpatvāt | svātmā tu parameśvaro na  vidhipūrvako-vidhipariprāpitatvābhāvāt | nahi tadanuddeśana  kiṃcitpravartate | tena vidhipariprāpitendrādidevatoddeśeṣu  sarveṣu sa svātmā viśvāvabhāsanasvabhāvaḥ  taduddeśyadevatāvabhāsabhittisthānīyatayaivāhamahamikayā  satatāvabhāsamānaḥ sraksūtrakalpaḥ satatoddiṣṭa iti  yuktisiddhametat māmeva yajanti-avidhipūrvakatvāt | mukhyabhūtamatprāptiphalasya tānprati kartrabhiprāyatvaṃ nāsti  apitu parimitadakṣiṇāsthānīyendrādipadamātraprāptereva  yājakavaccaritārthatvameṣām-iti prathayituṃ parasmaipadam | yaduktaṃ mayaiva-   vadānveda na veda śāṃbhavapadaṃ dūyeta nirvedavān svagārthī  yajamānatāṃ pratijahajjāto yajanyājakaḥ | sarvāḥ  karmarasapravāhaprasarāḥ saṃvitsravantyo'khilā-  stvāmānandamahāmbudhiṃ vidadhate nāprāpya pūrṇāṃ sthitim | iti

plain_english: Thus, one who knows in the stated order finds even an offering to Indra and other gods to be an offering to the supreme lord; every other action too becomes worship of the great lord as one's own self. Therefore whatever you do, eat, offer, give, or practice as austerity, O son of Kunti, do that as an offering to me.
sanskrit_cite: evaṃ ya uktakrameṇa vetti-tasyendrādidevatāyāgo'pi  parameśvarayāga iti yadapyanyatkarma tadapi  maheśvarasvātmārcanarūpaṃ tasyaiva sarvatroddeśāt-ityāha   yatkaroṣi yadaśnāsi yajjuhoṣi dadāsi yat | yattapasyasi kaunteya  tatkuruṣva madarpaṇam

plain_english: Thus you will be freed from the bonds of action by auspicious and inauspicious fruits; united with renunciation-yoga and freed, you will approach me. Worshippers of other gods have limited desires and diminish the fruit; therefore you, by the previously stated teaching order, do contemplation as offering to me, as me-ness. This indeed is renunciation-yoga, already stated extensively and almost clearly before.
sanskrit_cite: śubhāśubhaphalairevaṃ mokṣyase karmabandhanaiḥ | saṃnyāsayogayuktātmā vimukto māmupaiṣyasi | devatāntarayājino yato mitamanorathāḥ phalaṃ laghayanti atastvaṃ  sarve prāguktopadeśakrameṇa madarpaṇaṃ-manmayatvena bhāvanaṃ kuru | eṣa eva ca saṃnyāsayogaḥ | iti vistīrṇaṃ vispaṣṭaprāyaṃ  purastādeva

plain_english: I am equal among all beings; to me none is hateful, none dear. But those who worship me with devotion are in me, and I too am in them.
sanskrit_cite: samo'haṃ sarvabhūteṣu na me dveṣyo'sti na priyaḥ | ye bhajanti tu  māṃ bhaktyā mayi te teṣu cā'pyaham

plain_english: Even if someone is of very bad conduct, if he worships me with undivided devotion, he should indeed be considered a saint, for he is rightly resolved.
sanskrit_cite: api cet sudurācāro bhajate māmananyabhāk | sādhureva sa mantavyaḥ  samyagvyavasito hi saḥ

plain_english: Quickly one becomes righteous and attains eternal peace; O son of Kunti, declare that my devotee does not perish. I declare it. Because the Lord has declared it, this reasoned meaning becomes firmly established.
sanskrit_cite: kṣipraṃ bhavati dharmātmā śaśvacchāntiṃ nigacchati | kaunteya  pratijānīhi na madbhaktaḥ praṇaśyati | pratijāne iti-yuktiyukto'yamartho  bhagavatpratijñātatvātsuṣṭhutamāṃ dṛḍho bhavati

plain_english: O Partha, even those of sinful birth, women, vaishyas, and shudras who take refuge in me indeed go to the supreme destination.
sanskrit_cite: māṃ hi pārtha vyapāśritya ye'pi syuḥ pāpayonayaḥ | striyo  vaiśyāstathā śūdrāste'pi yānti parāṃ gatim

plain_english: How much more so holy brahmins and devoted royal sages; having obtained this impermanent, unhappy world, worship me.
sanskrit_cite: kiṃ punarbrāhmaṇāḥ puṇyā bhaktā rājarṣayastathā | anityamasukhaṃ lokamimaṃ prāpya bhajasva mām

plain_english: Fix your mind on me, become my devotee and worshipper, bow to me, and you will come to me alone. Even those born in sinful wombs, animals, birds, reptiles, women, vaiśyas, śūdras, and dependent persons who take refuge in me worship me alone. The supremely compassionate Lord's deeds, such as the liberation of the elephant king, are heard in thousands. Some interpret the verse as praise of twice-born and kṣatriyas, not as an intent of liberation for women and others; they fragment the Lord's all-gracious power and cannot endure His supreme compassion. The Lord has no enemy and no dear one, even one of evil conduct. Other clear statements are contradicted by those who forcibly introduce difference into the nondual essence of the Lord and ignore scriptural contradictions. When questioned, those deeply immersed in caste obsession, envy, shame, and crooked gaze impute comic rasa to the false prattle of all people. The commentary makes all auspicious.
sanskrit_cite: manmanā bhava madbhakto madyājī māṃ namaskuru | māmevaiṣyasi  yuktvaivamātmānaṃ matparāyaṇaḥ | pāpayonayaḥ-paśupakṣisarīsṛpādayaḥ | striya ityajñāḥ | vaiśyā iti-kṛṣyādikarmāntararatāḥ | śūdrā iti-kārtsnyena  vaidikakriyānadhikṛtāḥ paratantravṛttayaśca | te'pi madāśritā  māmeva yajante | (gajendramokṣaṇādīni caritāni hi  paramakāruṇikasya bhagavataḥ sahasraśaḥ śrūyante) | kimaṅga  punaretadviparītavṛttayaḥ | kecidācakṣate-dvijarājanyapraśaṃsāparametadvākyaṃ natu  stryādiṣvapavargaprāptitātparyeṇa-iti | te hi bhagavataḥ  sarvānugrāhikāṃ śaktiṃ mitaviṣayatayā khaṇḍayantaḥ tathā  parameśvarasya paramakṛpālutvamasahamānāḥ na me dveṣyo'sti na  priyaḥ api cetsudurācāraḥ ityādīnyanyāni  caivaṃprakārasphuṭārthapratipādakāni vākyāni virodhayanto  niratiśayayuktiprapañcasādhitādvaitabhagavattattve bhedaliṅgaṃ  balādevānayanto anyāṃścāgamavirodhānacetayamānāḥ kathamidaṃ  kathamidam-iti paryanuyujyamānā yadi  paramantargabhīkṛtajātyādimahāgrahāviṣṭāntaḥkaraṇāḥ  mātsaryāvahitthalajjājihmīkṛtāvāṅmukhadṛṣṭayaḥ samagrasya  janasyāsatpralāpina iti hāsyarasaviṣayabhāvamātmanyāropayanti | yatpūrvaiva vyākhyā sarvasya karoti śivamiti śivam

plain_english: Here is the summary verse: in non-dual Brahman the supreme Power, full of grace to all, unfolds; therefore one should strive to attain it.
sanskrit_cite: atra saṃgrahaślokaḥ   advaite brahmaṇi parā sarvānugrahaśālinī | śāktirvijṛmbhate  tena yatanīyaṃ tadāptaye | iti śrīmahāmaheśvarācāryavaryarājānakābhinavaguptapādaviracite  śrīmadbhagavadgītārthasaṃgrahe navamo'dhyāyaḥ
